# H-Bridge

Drives one channel of an H-bridge device (for example a DRV8962 motor driver): sets the speed and direction of a motor, or brakes or coasts it. The bridge itself (pins, topology, current limit, power source) is set up in the device; the block only steers it.

## Pins and settings

| | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Drive (float, optional) | Speed and direction in **percent**: -100..100 for a full bridge (negative = reverse), 0..100 for a half bridge. Overrides the **Drive** setting. Used when the action is *Drive*. |
| Device | The H-bridge to steer. Only H-bridge devices are listed. |
| Channel | The bridge channel of that device (a DRV8962 has four half bridges or two full bridges). |
| Action | What the block does while it is enabled: *Drive* (follow the Drive input), *Brake* (short the motor terminals) or *Coast* (release the motor). |
| Drive | The value used while the Drive input is unwired. |
| When not active | What the bridge does while the block is not enabled: *coast*, *brake* or *hold* (leave it as it is). |
| ENO | True while the bridge follows the block this pass. |

## Behaviour

- The bridge is only commanded when the value (or the action) **changes**.
- A value outside the bridge's range is an error and the bridge does not move; it is never clamped. A magnitude below 0.5 % brakes.
- The bridge needs power: select the supply source of its power mux and make sure the rail is on.
- To drive a motor both ways with one block, wire a signed value to **Drive**; to stop it with a brake, switch the action or disable the block with *When not active* set to *brake*.
